method: The page divides total facility energy by IT equipment energy, the definition The Green Grid gives for power usage effectiveness (PUE); the quotient is reported to two decimals and its inverse, data center infrastructure efficiency (DCiE), as the IT share in percent. Total facility energy covers everything the data center draws: the IT equipment itself plus power delivery (UPS, switchgear, generators, PDUs, batteries and distribution losses), cooling (chillers, cooling towers, pumps, CRAHs, CRACs, DX units) and miscellaneous loads such as lighting, so the ratio can never fall below 1.0 and a facility with no overhead at all would score exactly 1.0. The overhead is the facility total less the IT load, also expressed as a share of the facility total and as overhead per unit of IT load (PUE minus one). The target field compares the facility with a chosen PUE: the facility figure the same IT load would need at that target is IT load multiplied by the target, and the difference is reported as an absolute amount and as a share of the facility total, so a facility below the target is shown as a saving. Figures may be entered as energy over a period (kWh) or as average power (kW); because the same window cancels in the ratio, PUE is identical either way, but the period matters for PUE itself, which the Green Grid defines as an energy metric and recommends reporting over a period rather than as an instantaneous reading, since the ratio moves with the weather, the load and the way the plant is run. Thousands separators and spaces are accepted in either figure. Both inputs must be greater than zero and no more than 1,000,000,000,000, and the facility total may not be smaller than the IT load: that combination is physically impossible rather than worth reporting, so it is refused with an explanation instead of being clamped. The target is limited to 1.0-20.0. Comparing figures measured at different levels (the paper's L1 to L3 meter placements) or over different windows is not valid, and PUE says nothing about how much useful work the IT equipment does.

sources.title: The Green Grid Association: PUE: A Comprehensive Examination of the Metric, White Paper #49 (2012) - PUE is total facility energy divided by IT equipment energy (Equation 1), total facility energy includes the IT load plus UPS, PDUs, batteries and distribution losses, chillers, CRAHs and CRACs and lighting, DCiE is its inverse, PUE is defined as an energy metric reported over a period, values run from 1.0 upward with 1.6 or better achievable by design, and measurements differ by the L1-L3 meter placements
